sites.name: Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum and Terracotta Army
sites.what: Burial complex of China's first emperor near Xi'an, with the Terracotta Army pits (UNESCO World Heritage).

access.opening: 16 March to 15 November 8.30 am to 5 pm; 16 November to 15 March 8.30 am to 4.30 pm; holiday hours by notice
access.tickets: Real-name online booking only through the museum's website, WeChat account or 兵马俑票务在线; bring the original ID (passport) used to book

lore.text: Popular lore says the unopened tomb holds rivers of mercury and crossbow traps, drawing on Sima Qian's ancient account.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

ancient-sites-and-mysteries.evidence: Official pages; read directly unless marked search snapshot.

layers.authority: Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum (Terracotta Army)
layers.process: Visits need a real-name reservation, including for foreign and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan visitors. Book on the museum's ticketing site (bmy.com.cn) using a second-generation ID or passport details, or through its WeChat accounts 'Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum' or 'Terracotta Warriors Ticketing Online'. The scenic area's maximum is 65,000 people a day; ticket sales stop when it is reached. Bring the original ID document (a passport counts) to be checked at the gate. Opening hours: 8:30 to 17:00 from 16 March to 15 November; 8:30 to 16:30 from 16 November to 15 March.

sources.title: Visitor guide: ticketing and opening hours
sources.supports: real-name reservation, foreign visitors, 65,000 daily cap, passport check (read directly 2026-11-06)

zone-requirements.note: Lead time is not published; 0 is a placeholder. Huashan and the Xi'an smoking rules were not confirmed from an official page and are not recorded.

laws.rule: Visitors must keep to public order and manners, look after tourism facilities, resources and the environment, respect local customs, culture and religion, follow safety and health rules, and not harm local residents or disturb other visitors (article 10). Visitors on tourist coaches and boats are asked to follow safety warnings and use seat belts and safety gear (article 43).
laws.penalty_signal: No fine on the visitor is set in the article read; breaches fall under the other laws that apply.
laws.heading: 陕西省旅游条例 (Shaanxi Province Tourism Regulation)

laws.rule: Xi'an City Wall: banned acts in the protected area include carving, scribbling or pasting on the wall, fishing or angling in the moat without approval, dumping sewage or rubbish, driving piles or taking bricks and soil, and storing flammables (article 10). Filming for film, TV or advertising, or holding a large event, needs approval, and doing business on the wall is not allowed without approval.
laws.penalty_signal: Carving or scribbling, or fishing in the moat: warning and CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66). Dumping sewage or rubbish: CNY 200 to 1,000 (about A$42.66 to A$213). Piling, taking bricks or soil: CNY 500 to 1,000 (about A$107 to A$213). Unapproved building work or blasting with serious results: CNY 50,000 to 500,000 (about A$10,666 to A$106,662). Unapproved filming: CNY 5,000 to 50,000 (about A$1,067 to A$10,666). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 西安城墙保护条例 (Xian City Wall Protection Regulation)

laws.rule: Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum: within the protected area it is banned to dig sand or soil, dump waste or rubbish, photograph where photography is banned, store flammable or explosive items, and paste, scribble on, carve or climb the relics, protective fittings and markers (article 12). Boundary markers may not be moved or damaged.
laws.penalty_signal: Warning, repair, and possibly CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66) (articles 23 and 24). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 陕西省秦始皇陵保护条例 (Shaanxi Province Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum Protection Regulation)

laws.rule: Xi'an: a dog must be on a lead of no more than two metres, held by an adult, and the owner must clean up droppings (article 27). Dogs are banned from government offices, hospitals, schools, heritage sites, museums, libraries, sports and entertainment venues, restaurants, shops, hotels, buses, rail transit, taxis and their waiting areas, city squares, parks, main roads and pedestrian streets (article 28). Guide dogs and assistance dogs are exempt.
laws.penalty_signal: Taking a dog into a banned place: CNY 50 to 200 (about A$10.67 to A$42.66) per dog (article 52). Droppings not cleared: CNY 50 to 100 (about A$10.67 to A$21.33) (article 51). Lead, noise and similar breaches: CNY 200 to 500 (about A$42.66 to A$107) (article 51). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
